title: Software Architecture & Product Architecture
summary: Turn product capabilities, quality attributes, organizational boundaries and operational constraints into evolvable technical architecture.

modules.title: Architecture reasoning & trade-offs
modules.summary: Treat architecture as consequential decisions under constraints rather than diagram aesthetics.
modules.why: Senior architects explain why a design fits this product, scale, team and failure cost—not merely which pattern it resembles.

units.title: Architecture-significant decisions
units.summary: Identify choices whose cost/risk persists across many future changes.
units.challenge: Given a feature backlog, separate local implementation choices from architecture-significant decisions.
units.evidence: Decision inventory ranked by reversibility and consequence.

units.title: Trade-off analysis & explicit assumptions
units.summary: Compare alternatives on measurable consequences rather than preference.
units.challenge: Compare relational DB, document DB and event-sourced model for one bounded problem.
units.evidence: Trade-off matrix with assumptions and trigger conditions for revisiting the decision.

units.title: Architecture fitness functions & evolutionary constraints
units.summary: Encode important architecture properties as observable/testable constraints where possible.
units.challenge: Define five automated/manual fitness functions for the capstone architecture.
units.evidence: Executable checks or review criteria tied to architecture goals.

modules.title: Quality attributes & non-functional requirements
modules.summary: Translate words like scalable, secure and reliable into scenarios, measurements and trade-offs.
modules.why: Unmeasurable NFRs cannot guide architecture or acceptance decisions.

units.title: Quality-attribute scenarios
units.summary: Specify stimulus, environment, response and measurable response measure.
units.challenge: Rewrite ten vague NFRs into measurable scenarios.
units.evidence: Quality-attribute scenario catalog with acceptance metrics.

units.title: Conflicting quality attributes
units.summary: Recognize that optimizing one quality can degrade another.
units.challenge: Prioritize quality attributes for consumer chat vs regulated payment service.
units.evidence: Utility/trade-off table explaining different architecture outcomes.

units.title: Architecture tactics for quality attributes
units.summary: Connect requirements to reusable design tactics without prematurely selecting a technology.
units.challenge: Map each capstone NFR to candidate tactics and their side effects.
units.evidence: Tactic map with validation method for each requirement.

modules.title: Strategic Domain-Driven Design
modules.summary: Discover business capabilities and boundaries before choosing service boundaries.
modules.why: Technical decomposition fails when it slices by tables or CRUD operations rather than business ownership/change patterns.

units.title: Domain modeling & ubiquitous language
units.summary: Build shared vocabulary around business concepts, rules and events.
units.challenge: Create a domain glossary for collaboration/product work management without technical terms.
units.evidence: Glossary and ambiguous-term resolutions validated against example workflows.

units.title: Bounded contexts & ownership boundaries
units.summary: Define models that are internally consistent and independently evolvable.
units.challenge: Partition the capstone into bounded contexts and challenge every boundary with change scenarios.
units.evidence: Context map with reasons each concept belongs where it does.

units.title: Context mapping & integration relationships
units.summary: Make dependencies between contexts explicit and choose integration relationships deliberately.
units.challenge: Map identity, work management, notifications and analytics dependencies.
units.evidence: Context map labeling relationship type and coupling risk.

modules.title: Tactical DDD & aggregate design
modules.summary: Model invariants inside bounded contexts without creating giant object graphs.
modules.why: Aggregates are consistency boundaries, not collections of every related entity.

units.title: Entities, value objects & domain services
units.summary: Choose identity and behavior placement based on domain semantics.
units.challenge: Model task, status, due date, membership and permission concepts without anemic data bags.
units.evidence: Domain model with invariants and tests independent of persistence/framework.

units.title: Aggregates & consistency boundaries
units.summary: Keep synchronous invariants local and cross-aggregate coordination explicit.
units.challenge: Redesign a giant Project aggregate that locks too much state.
units.evidence: Aggregate boundaries with invariant/transaction rationale.

units.title: Domain events & side-effect separation
units.summary: Expose meaningful state transitions without coupling domain code to infrastructure.
units.challenge: Model task completion triggering audit/notification/analytics without direct infrastructure calls from entity.
units.evidence: Sequence from domain transition to committed event publication.

modules.title: Modular monolith architecture
modules.summary: Achieve strong internal boundaries and independent ownership without paying distributed-system cost prematurely.
modules.why: A well-designed monolith can support large teams and future extraction while simplifying transactions, testing and operations.

units.title: Module boundaries & dependency rules
units.summary: Enforce one-way dependencies and hide module internals.
units.challenge: Create work/identity/notification modules and make cross-module internal imports fail CI.
units.evidence: Module dependency graph and automated boundary checks.

units.title: Data ownership inside a monolith
units.summary: Avoid shared-table coupling even when one physical database is used.
units.challenge: Prevent notification code from querying work-management tables directly.
units.evidence: Data-access ownership rules and integration interface.

units.title: Designing for extraction without pre-distribution
units.summary: Preserve seams that can later become network boundaries if real pressure emerges.
units.challenge: Identify which module could become a service and simulate extraction cost.
units.evidence: Extraction readiness assessment and reasons not to extract others.

modules.title: Microservices decomposition & service ownership
modules.summary: Split runtime services only where business/operational autonomy justifies distributed complexity.
modules.why: Bad microservice boundaries amplify coupling into network latency, duplicated data and cross-team coordination.

units.title: Service-boundary forces & decomposition strategies
units.summary: Balance business capability, change coupling, scale, security and team ownership.
units.challenge: Score candidate service boundaries for the capstone and reject at least two weak splits.
units.evidence: Boundary decision matrix with coupling metrics/examples.

units.title: Database-per-service & data ownership
units.summary: Keep service autonomy without hidden shared-database coupling.
units.challenge: Replace a cross-service SQL join with explicit ownership and read model/API composition.
units.evidence: Before/after data flow and consistency semantics.

units.title: Microservice operational & organizational cost
units.summary: Account for deployment, observability, incident and platform overhead per service.
units.challenge: Compare 5-service and 50-service decomposition for a 3-team organization.
units.evidence: Total-cost/cognitive-load ADR and minimum platform prerequisites.

modules.title: Architecture styles & when they fit
modules.summary: Understand runtime/deployment styles as combinations of forces rather than competing religions.
modules.why: Styles such as event-driven, serverless and CQRS address different constraints and can coexist.

units.title: Layered, hexagonal & clean architecture
units.summary: Control dependency direction and isolate infrastructure from core behavior.
units.challenge: Implement one feature in layered and ports/adapters forms and compare testing/change cost.
units.evidence: Dependency diagrams and trade-off memo.

units.title: Event-driven, serverless, CQRS & event sourcing
units.summary: Recognize styles built around asynchronous events, managed functions and separate models.
units.challenge: Choose styles for notification, audit history and image processing without applying one style globally.
units.evidence: Capability-to-style map with rejected alternatives.

units.title: Cell-based, bulkhead & space-based scaling concepts
units.summary: Reduce blast radius and centralized bottlenecks through partitioned deployment units.
units.challenge: Design isolated cells for a SaaS product with thousands of tenants.
units.evidence: Cell topology, routing and rebalancing/failure analysis.

modules.title: Multi-tenant SaaS architecture
modules.summary: Design tenant identity, isolation, fairness, encryption, migration and residency across every layer.
modules.why: Multi-tenancy is a cross-cutting architecture property, not just adding tenant_id to tables.

units.title: Tenant identity & request context propagation
units.summary: Resolve tenant safely and propagate it through synchronous/async work.
units.challenge: Implement tenant resolution and prove user cannot spoof another tenant through headers/body.
units.evidence: Request/event context sequence and negative tests.

units.title: Shared schema, schema-per-tenant & database-per-tenant
units.summary: Choose data isolation model from scale, compliance and operations.
units.challenge: Design basic/enterprise/regulated tenant tiers with different data isolation.
units.evidence: Isolation tier matrix and migration path between tiers.

units.title: Noisy-neighbor protection, quotas & workload isolation
units.summary: Ensure one tenant cannot consume shared compute/cache/DB/queue capacity unfairly.
units.challenge: Protect shared report/export workers from one high-volume tenant.
units.evidence: Tenant-level admission/scheduling policy and load test.

units.title: Tenant encryption, residency & lifecycle
units.summary: Support per-tenant keys, region placement, export/deletion and moves.
units.challenge: Move an enterprise tenant from shared US storage to isolated EU storage with minimal downtime.
units.evidence: Tenant migration/runbook including cache/search/files/backups.

modules.title: Enterprise & third-party integration architecture
modules.summary: Integrate unreliable external systems while protecting internal domain models and data ownership.
modules.why: Vendors have independent availability, schemas and change cycles; integration boundaries must absorb that instability.

units.title: Adapters & anti-corruption layers
units.summary: Translate external concepts into internal language without contaminating domain models.
units.challenge: Integrate two ticket vendors with different status/user models behind internal semantics.
units.evidence: Mapping model and list of intentionally unabstracted differences.

units.title: API, webhook, polling, files & message exchange
units.summary: Choose integration channel from timeliness, reliability and vendor capability.
units.challenge: Design an HR-user-provisioning integration where vendor supports inconsistent capabilities.
units.evidence: Channel decision matrix and fallback path.

units.title: Vendor failure, reconciliation & source-of-truth rules
units.summary: Converge state after timeouts, outages and missed callbacks.
units.challenge: Design payment/provider integration where create response is lost and webhook may be delayed.
units.evidence: State machine and reconciliation strategy for uncertain outcomes.

modules.title: Architecture evolution & large-scale migrations
modules.summary: Change systems incrementally while old/new paths coexist and production remains available.
modules.why: Most architect work is evolution of existing systems, not greenfield design.

units.title: Strangler, branch-by-abstraction & incremental replacement
units.summary: Move capability gradually while preserving a stable facade or routing point.
units.challenge: Migrate one monolith capability to a service without a big-bang release.
units.evidence: Migration checkpoints each independently deployable/demoable.

units.title: Shadow traffic, dual run & comparison
units.summary: Validate new behavior before it becomes authoritative.
units.challenge: Validate a new search or pricing implementation using production shadow workload.
units.evidence: Comparison metrics and safe cutover criterion.

units.title: Cutover, backfill, reconciliation & rollback
units.summary: Treat migration as a stateful workflow with verification and recovery.
units.challenge: Design a zero-downtime database/service migration with 1TB data.
units.evidence: Detailed migration state machine, monitoring and abort conditions.

modules.title: Architecture documentation: C4, sequences, ADRs & RFCs
modules.summary: Make system intent and decisions inspectable for people who did not design it.
modules.why: Architecture that exists only in one engineer's head cannot scale across teams or survive turnover.

units.title: Context, container & component diagrams
units.summary: Show system boundaries at progressively useful levels without creating exhaustive UML.
units.challenge: Create context/container diagrams for the capstone and remove implementation noise.
units.evidence: C4 diagrams understandable without verbal explanation.

units.title: Sequence, data-flow & trust-boundary diagrams
units.summary: Show runtime interactions and movement of data/security context.
units.challenge: Diagram login, task update+notification and file upload including failures.
units.evidence: Diagrams used as inputs to threat/failure review.

units.title: ADRs & RFCs
units.summary: Record context, alternatives, decisions, risks and rollout instead of only final design.
units.challenge: Write an RFC for introducing event streaming or tenant isolation.
units.evidence: Reviewed 4-6 page RFC plus final ADR capturing decision and revisit triggers.

modules.title: Architecture risk, FMEA & review practice
modules.summary: Review proposed systems for failure modes, hidden coupling and operational gaps before launch.
modules.why: Good architecture review finds the expensive problems while they are still cheap to change.

units.title: Failure-mode and dependency analysis
units.summary: Enumerate how components fail, detection, impact and mitigation.
units.challenge: Perform FMEA on notification pipeline and identity dependency.
units.evidence: Risk table with prioritized design changes.

units.title: Architecture review question framework
units.summary: Systematically challenge data ownership, consistency, capacity, security, operability and evolution.
units.challenge: Review an unfamiliar architecture using a structured question set and identify top five unresolved risks.
units.evidence: Review memo distinguishing blockers, follow-ups and accepted risks.

units.title: Decision follow-through & architecture governance
units.summary: Ensure review decisions become implementation checks rather than meeting notes.
units.challenge: Convert an RFC's assumptions/risks into CI checks, dashboards and launch gates.
units.evidence: Traceability map from decision to verification artifact.

modules.title: Product discovery & requirements for architects
modules.summary: Understand user jobs, workflows and business rules before optimizing technical structure.
modules.why: A product architect must connect architecture to what users are actually trying to accomplish and what the business must protect.

units.title: Users, jobs-to-be-done & critical journeys
units.summary: Identify primary actors, goals, critical paths and failure consequences.
units.challenge: Map onboarding→project creation→collaboration→notification journeys for three personas.
units.evidence: Journey map showing technical implications and critical SLO/security points.

units.title: Functional requirements, invariants & domain rules
units.summary: Separate user-visible capabilities from hidden business correctness rules.
units.challenge: Turn a vague 'project sharing' feature into states, invariants, permissions and failure cases.
units.evidence: Requirement/domain-rule specification with example scenarios.

units.title: Ambiguity, assumptions & decision questions
units.summary: Drive clarity without blocking progress when product information is incomplete.
units.challenge: Take an ambiguous system-design prompt/product brief and produce the highest-value clarification questions.
units.evidence: Assumption log with impact if wrong and validation plan.

modules.title: HCI, UX & client constraints for architects
modules.summary: Understand interaction, accessibility, offline/mobile and perceived-latency concerns that reshape backend/system design.
modules.why: Architecture choices should support user experience rather than forcing the UI to compensate for poor contracts/latency models.

units.title: Interaction latency & perceived performance
units.summary: Relate user feedback timing to synchronous/asynchronous architecture.
units.challenge: Redesign a 5-second synchronous action into responsive user states without lying about success.
units.evidence: UX/backend state machine including pending, confirmed and failed states.

units.title: Offline, mobile & unreliable network constraints
units.summary: Design sync and conflict behavior for clients that disappear/reconnect.
units.challenge: Design mobile task editing under intermittent connectivity.
units.evidence: Sync/conflict protocol and data-storage decisions.

units.title: Accessibility, localization & internationalization architecture
units.summary: Account for text direction, locale, timezone, accessibility and content expansion at system boundaries.
units.challenge: Make reminders/dates/search work correctly across locales/timezones and accessible UI.
units.evidence: Internationalization architecture and representative edge-case tests.

modules.title: Technical product economics: build/buy, cost/value & roadmap
modules.summary: Make technical investments proportional to business value, risk and option value.
modules.why: The most sophisticated architecture is wrong if it delays value or creates operating cost without corresponding benefit.

units.title: Build vs buy vs partner decisions
units.summary: Evaluate strategic differentiation, control, lock-in, compliance and lifecycle cost.
units.challenge: Decide whether to build identity, search and notification infrastructure for the capstone.
units.evidence: Three build/buy decision records with different outcomes.

units.title: Architecture investment & option value
units.summary: Fund reliability/platform/migration work through quantified risk or future option value.
units.challenge: Prioritize five architecture investments against feature work using explicit value/risk assumptions.
units.evidence: Prioritization model and decision narrative.

units.title: Technical roadmaps & decision gates
units.summary: Sequence architecture evolution so each checkpoint produces useful capability and evidence.
units.challenge: Create a roadmap from modular monolith to selectively distributed architecture where every checkpoint is demoable.
units.evidence: Roadmap with dependencies, exit criteria and stop/go decisions.

modules.title: Team topology, ownership & socio-technical architecture
modules.summary: Align system boundaries with communication/ownership patterns and reduce cross-team coordination cost.
modules.why: Architecture and organization influence each other; unclear ownership creates shared-service bottlenecks and unsafe changes.

units.title: Conway's Law & team/system boundaries
units.summary: Use organizational communication needs as an input to decomposition.
units.challenge: Compare system decomposition for one team vs eight autonomous teams.
units.evidence: Team/system map and expected coordination hotspots.

units.title: Service/platform ownership operating model
units.summary: Define who builds, deploys, operates, secures and evolves each component.
units.challenge: Create ownership model for platform, identity and product services.
units.evidence: Ownership matrix covering build/run/change/incident responsibilities.

units.title: Platform vs product boundaries
units.summary: Centralize reusable capabilities without forcing domain-specific behavior into generic platforms.
units.challenge: Decide whether notifications, authorization and search belong in platform or product teams.
units.evidence: Capability placement ADRs with consumer/ownership implications.
